Confirmed. Your last turn means your last turn.

Similarly, if you Sudden your predator's Information Highway and then
(on that same turn) she puts a First Tradition in play and you skip a
few turns, you
still loses a master phase action on your "next" turn (since you played
a master: out-of-turn since your "last" turn").

See Lupus Australis's note to that effect in this thread:

To be honest, I think this card makes "Choir Decks" worse.

Before this card, the prey of the DoC player would not bother to block
most of the inferior Choir actions, most of the time.
Now, just because this card exists, it encourages the prey (and maybe
predator) to attempt to block every single inferior action, so that it
can't build up over 2 turns for a devastating effect.
Which means that the Choir Deck needs to allocate more resources to
getting successful actions through. And you can only Dare the Dawn so
many times before your entire crypt is in torpor...

On the other hand, I think this card encourages "casual Choirs" to be
tossed in to a Daughter deck. 6-8 Choirs and 1 Hanging Fermata will be
enough to add the extra "spice" to a Daughter Vote deck or whatnot...

Just my opinion.

> Now, just because this card exists, it encourages the prey (and maybe
> predator) to attempt to block every single inferior action, so that it
> can't build up over 2 turns for a devastating effect.

But on the other hand, you'll get more mileage against casual blockers
with Hanging Fermata.

Last I've played a Choir deck, I'd usually have 4 Daughters ready at
some point to strap a 6-point Choir. Preys with casual intercept either
would save the intercept for the last Choir at superior, or if they
think they don't have enough intercept to stop that, would use the few
they have to stop one or two inferior Choirs by the [mel] Daughters to
diminish the damage. In this situation, at best, the ideal Choir Damage
would drop to 4 or even 2, at the expense of tapping all minions. At
worst, the prey would succeed to block the last Choir, so no pool
damage this turn.

Hanging Fermata resolves both problems, making it worth the turn you've
spent building inferior Choirs even if you think the last one will be
blocked, or for wasting your prey's casual intercept and free yourself
to burst through next round. As a side effect, it makes preys who can
consistedly block Choir actions more aware that they should do so, but
that's fine for me since it already happens somewhat anyway. Choirs do
pool damage that's not bounceable or reduceable, and since most wall
decks also pack some bounce or bleed reduction as defense, it's already
crucial for them to block Choirs.

> Which means that the Choir Deck needs to allocate more resources to
> getting successful actions through. And you can only Dare the Dawn so
> many times before your entire crypt is in torpor...

I usually go for all that's possible to throw in to pass the actions
anyway. I've even considered throwing in some Polaris Coach.

> On the other hand, I think this card encourages "casual Choirs" to be
> tossed in to a Daughter deck. 6-8 Choirs and 1 Hanging Fermata will be
> enough to add the extra "spice" to a Daughter Vote deck or whatnot...

I don't know if it's worth it with these particular numbers, though I
agree with the general idea. Hanging Fermata only maintains the Choirs
for a turn, so once you play it you'd still need to have at least 2
Choirs played *this turn* and draw at least 2 more in the next turn to
be worth it (4 actions to remove 6 pool, instead of 4 bleeds for 1).
6-8 Choirs doesn't strike me as a good number to ensure you'll
have/draw/play 4x of them in quick succession (2 turns).

But adjusting the numbers, 2 Hanging Fermata could turn one's 12-14
Choirs useful; just tackle another strategy in it (political or not),
and you're good to go.

best,

Fabio "Sooner" Macedo

Messages.Author: Fabio 'Sooner' Macedo
Messages.Body:


True, but in turn it requires you card slots, while single bleeds don't
(not to mention permableed which require fewer card slots for a better
result, now that Angela can get a Heart of City and such).

About the stealth, no Choir deck I've seen so far relies on getting the
actions through without a reasonable amount of extra stealth. So the
deck will probably have some stealth to pass the bleeds anyway. Not to
mention that without Hanging Fermata, you can have a turn like this:
- tap all your minions for Choirs
- get blocked at last Choir
And your prey only needs one untapped minion to foil the whole turn of
yours, who is tapped out by now for nothing.

If you bled with all minions, your prey would have a harder time to
block them all and/or have enough bounce or bleed reduction cards to
make you waste your whole turn for naught.

In the end, Choir is indeed better than plain regular bleeding, but
only when the most successful scenarios are compared - and it has to
be, because it involves way more potential for waste of resources with
no gain at all.

best,

Fabio "Sooner" Macedo

Messages.Author: pd...@lightlink.com
Messages.Body:
Jozxyqk wrote:
> To be honest, I think this card makes "Choir Decks" worse.

I don't know if it is fair to say it makes the "worse", but as cool as
the card seems, I agree that it is probably not as good as one would
initially think. Assuming you have 4 Daughters and no one blocks you on
any of your Choir actions:

-With Hanging, over 2 turns, you do (4 Choir +3 Choir+ Superior)14 pool
damage.

-Without Hanging, over 2 turns, you do (3 Choir + Superior + 3 Choir +
Superior) 12 pool damage.

Basically, you get to spend an MPA to do 2 extra pool damage. Which
isn't that huge.

What it strikes me as most useful for is having a couple in the deck
just in case you try and top deck for another Choir to play at superior
(i.e. you have 1 choir in your hand. Play it, and hope to draw another.
If you do, play a second and try to draw a third, etc.), and if you
don't, you can save them all till next turn. But in that instance, why
not just replace the Hangings with more Choirs...

-Peter

Messages.Author: Rehlow
Messages.Body:


I agree. I would call Hanging Fermata your "get out of jail free card."
If your Superior Choir has been blocked, you don't lose the whole turn.

Relying on it to combo two turns of Choirs together generally just
isn't worth it. Over two turns, its only two more pool damage and if
your superior Choir delivery method is Daring the Dawn, its one less
trip to torpor, but since the first half can be lost by a Sudden
Reversal, I don't think building a deck around Choirs over 2 turns is
worth it.

The only useable if you didn't play one last turn actually protects you
from being an idiot and planning to string them together over several
turns. If that were possible, you would get a good three turns of Choir
together and then someone would Sudden Reverse your next Hanging
Fermata and you'd lose it all.

> and maybe Sponteneous Power will add another vamp able to put the choirs
> into play. This might make the choir deck playable.

I think it could be useful in a Daughters with Embrace and Sanguine
Instruction deck going for the "ultimate" huge Choir. Previously, I
think this deck would have a terrible time with jamming, getting Choirs
early game when you want to be Embracing and Instructing, and then late
game, drawing Embraces and SI when you are trying to string together a
huge Choir. With Hanging Fermata, early game you can cycle Choirs by
playing the 1 to 2 you have and then "saving them" for next turn and
then during the following turn play another 1 or 2 at inferior and then
superior Choir activating the 3 or 4 in play. Late game, you have the
Hanging Fermata safety net in case your superior Choir is blocked
(provided no Sudden Reversal) you don't lose the whole turn's worth of
work.

Later,
~Rehlow
